newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - December 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - December 2.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Monday's edition of Daily Variety:

HOLLYWOOD - In Sony Pictures Entertainment President John Calley's first major outside executive hire, Turner Pictures president of production Amy Pascal will return to Columbia Pictures as president of the studio effective early next year, Columbia announced Sunday.

HOLLYWOOD - MCA's Universal Pictures brought its dueling volcano race with News Corp 's Fox 2000 to a boil on Friday by announcing a new February 7 release date for the studio's Dante's Peak. The date switch moves the Universal picture's release up by a full month, and it leapfrogs three weeks ahead of Fox's competing project, Volcano.

HOLLYWOOD - Oscar-winning writer Ron Bass has picked the first two projects he'll write for Sony 's TriStar Pictures under his new six-pic, $8 million deal with the studio: Cat and Mouse and The Code. It wasn't clear which will head into production first, but insiders said Cat is on a fast track.

HOLLYWOOD - Sexual politics - both gay and straight - and slicker-looking pictures mark the Sundance Film Festival, which runs January 16-26 in Park City, Utah, and boasts more films than ever in its lineup. Festival director Geoffrey Gilmore and his programming staff fielded a record 800 submissions for the 127 feature slots in the event, the world's leading showcase for American independent fare.
